messages:
sara: Quick sync — UX for automatic fallback policies: need to cover degrade modes, failure triggers, and audit. Thoughts?
kevin: +1. We should codify explicit modes: "cached-response", "reduced-llm" (smaller model), "stub", "rate-limited-queue". UI needs to show tradeoffs.
maria: Agree. Also need trigger types: error-rate (5xx%), latency p95>threshold, token-exhaustion, quota-breach, model-unavailable.
tony: Can we surface projected cost delta per mode in the UI? Customers always ask "what will this save vs quality loss".
sara: Yes — Redwood Optimize can estimate cost/latency/expected quality hit per route and we should surface that inline.
kevin: On audit: immutable timeline showing who enabled fallback, policy version, exact condition that fired, and links to traces/logs. Allow annotations.
maria: Add a "dry-run" option so policy only records "would have switched" without affecting traffic.
jamie: Also need per-customer and per-route overrides. Dedicated customers often want to opt-out of automated fallbacks.
sara: UX proposal: add a "Fallback rules" tab on Rollouts. Each rule shows: mode, triggers, scope, sensitivity (aggressive/lenient), last-fired reason, run-history log, and a "simulate" button.
kevin: For triggers allow composite AND/OR conditions, e.g., (p95>300ms AND error-rate>2%) OR model-unreachable. Keep an advanced mode for this.
maria: Suggest simple presets: "Fail open (low latency)", "Fail safe (maintain quality)", "Conservative" for quick onboarding.
tony: Telemetry: link to example trace with KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, and exact model variant used. Expose metric "fallback rate per 1k requests".
ops-bot: incident-bot: fallback rule prod/us-east/route-abc auto-switched at 19:12 UTC — triggered by p95=512ms. (automated)
sara: Need ability to retroactively replay a sampled request set under different fallback modes for regression testing (privacy-safe sampled).
kevin: Agree — include "simulate on historical window" that runs samples through chosen mode and reports quality delta.
maria: Questions: RBAC for enabling auto-fallback? Yes — only admins + release-engineers should toggle automatic rollbacks.
tony: UX microcopy: show clear "This will affect ~X% of requests" estimate and "Auto-revert after recovery window" toggle.
sara: Edge case: cascading fallbacks — if the smaller model is also unhealthy, fallback should attempt next priority (cached -> queue), with circuit-breaker cooldowns. Need priority ordering UI.
jamie: Also show cost delta over time if fallback persists >1h and bubble that to ops/billing.
kevin: Implementation note: store policy as versioned YAML. Example snippet: 
```
mode: reduced-llm
priority: 10
triggers:
  - type: latency
    metric: p95
    threshold_ms: 400
    window_s: 60
  - type: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 2
scope:
  routes: ["/chat/v1", "/generate"]
dry_run: true
```
maria: UX: when dry_run=true still emit "would-have" events in audit log, with a one-click promote-to-active action.
sara: Next steps: Kevin + Maria draft wireframe + canonical policy YAML. Tony to add cost-estimation fields. Jamie to list RBAC and enterprise opt-out rules. Sync tomorrow 09:30 PT.
kevin: I'll drop a Figma link after this.
maria: I'll add BigQuery sample queries to compute fallback-rate and cost delta.
sara: Thanks — good start. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: rollout-safety-checklist updated — require at least one canary before enabling auto-fallback globally.
